memories.text: Home is a small flat in Nairobi near Kilimani, and the traffic on Ngong Road is my daily punishment.
These days I'm at Savanna Health, mostly maintaining hospital equipment, and the hours are long.
I trained as a biomedical engineer, so anything with a sensor and a warranty ends up on my bench.
I'm hooked on thrillers right now, and I finish one every week on the bus.
Please explain things with a concrete example first; abstract definitions just bounce off me.
For the record, I'm not allergic to penicillin, my old clinic just mixed up my file once.
My younger brother Baraka lives in Arusha now and keeps sending me safari photos.
Our lab meeting is every Tuesday at 2pm, which ruins my lunch break.
Calibrating an infusion pump: zero the pressure sensor, run the 50 ml test bag, and log the deviation in the QA sheet before signing it off.
I'm now on Kesho, a project building a low-cost infusion pump for rural clinics.
Kesho is waiting on ethics approval before we can start the clinical trial.
I joined the Karura Running Club, and we do forest loops every Saturday at dawn.
Took a long weekend at Diani beach and finally learned to snorkel without panicking.
I carry an EpiPen because I'm seriously allergic to bee stings.
For chapati I knead the dough for ten minutes, rest it covered for an hour, then roll it into oiled coils before flattening.
Correction: the lab meeting moved to Wednesdays at 10am, which works much better.
My cousin's graduation party is going to be in Mombasa in December.
Kesho is owned by the Umoja Hospitals Trust, and they fund the whole prototype budget.
Good news on Kesho: the first patients were enrolled in the trial this week.
Drove out to Naivasha to watch the Safari Rally and came home covered in dust.
Change of plans for the graduation party, it's now in Nakuru because my aunt has a bigger compound there.
We adopted a tortoise from the shelter and it hides under the sofa all day.
I don't own a car, I take boda bodas and matatus everywhere.
Remind me to renew my work permit before the 1st of March.
Big move: I relocated to Kigali in June, and the hills here make every walk a workout.
I joined Mwangaza Robotics in June to lead their medical devices team.
Mwangaza Robotics is headquartered in Kampala, so I fly there about once a month.
I report to Peter Okello now, he founded the company's hardware lab.
Peter lives in Entebbe and jokes that he can see the airport from his garden.
I applied for a master's scholarship in Edinburgh, fingers crossed.
I've gone off thrillers completely; it's all historical fiction for me now.
The Kesho trial wrapped up last month and the results look really promising.
Spent the holidays in Zanzibar wandering around Stone Town.
I was offered the Edinburgh scholarship but deferred it by a year because of the new job.
My Sunday budget ritual: move 20 percent to savings first, pay the mobile money bills, and whatever is left is fun money.
I've never been to South America, but Patagonia is on my list.
Afrobeats is basically the soundtrack of my life, especially when I'm soldering.
I have to send the conference abstract before the 15th of September.
